source_excerpts.text:
# A paid attempt to repair a characteristic-two tensor algorithm

The proposed operation was **use the exact obstruction to lifting a tensor
decomposition to select a rank-preserving structural repair**, rather than
perform an undirected search followed by a lift test. The native target was
the published AlphaTensor 4-by-4 scheme with 47 products. The experiment did
not acquire a characteristic-zero scheme. It completely excludes the first
two local repair classes specified below, including intermediate rank 48.
This is a failed acquisition attempt with a useful exact boundary, not a new
matrix-multiplication upper/lower bound or a general algorithm-discovery gain.

The substantive general construction is the tangent-update compiler in §3.
The ordinary plus/flip operations and Hensel lifting are established methods;
see COSTS_AND_PRIOR.md. No priority for the compiler lemma is asserted.

## 1. Native input and the actual lifting question

The input is `factorizations_f2.npz`, supplied by Fawzi et al. in the official
google-deepmind/alphatensor repository, entry `4,4,4`. Its shape is
`(3,16,47)`. All entries are 0 or 1. Coordinates are cyclic: the third factor
represents the transpose of the product. Thus the target is

\[
 T_{4i+j,\,4j+k,\,4k+i}=1\quad(0\leq i,j,k<4),
\]

with every other coefficient zero. The acquired factors obey all 4096 tensor
equations modulo 2. Native byte identity/provenance are in SOURCES.json.

Write a decomposition as \(f=((a_r,b_r,c_r))_{r=1}^R\), and
\(F(f)=\sum_r a_r\otimes b_r\otimes c_r\). For a binary solution, choose its
0/1 integer representative \(\widetilde f\), and put

\[
 e_f=(T-F(\widetilde f))/2\pmod2,
 \qquad J_f=dF_f,\qquad I_f=\operatorname{im}J_f.                 \tag{1}
\]

All coefficients of \(T-F(\widetilde f)\) are even. The Jacobian image is the
sum, over terms, of

\[
 \mathcal T(a,b,c)=V_1\otimes b\otimes c
                  +a\otimes V_2\otimes c
                  +a\otimes b\otimes V_3.                       \tag{2}
\]

Since
\(F(\widetilde f+2x)=F(\widetilde f)+2J_fx\pmod4\), there is an
**unrestricted coefficient lift to Z/4** precisely when \(e_f\in I_f\).
No support, sign, magnitude, equal-factor or symmetry constraints are imposed
on the corrections. Native \(J_f\) has rank 2117, with 2256 variables; (1)
is inconsistent. That fixed-point fact was already known in the literature.

source_excerpts.text:
# Decision: the attempted local characteristic descent did not acquire an algorithm

We constructed a general exact tangent-update compiler for the ordinary
tensor plus move, then used it on the actual public AlphaTensor rank47
4-by-4 decomposition. The entire one-plus class fails unrestricted mod4
lifting: 12972 ordered moves,6486 distinct expanded states. All27924 flips
from those states fail even an enlarged necessary image test. No repaired
rank47 or rank48 characteristic-zero algorithm was acquired.

The complete two-move boundary is the useful negative outcome. It goes
beyond the already-known obstruction at the original point, but says
nothing about longer structural walks, another modular point, F3 searches,
ramified/even-denominator coefficients, or direct complex/rational searches.
Those alternatives are not ruled out. The construction does not justify
more undirected compute or a capability/novelty claim.

The native scheme is flip-free. Independent equation-row elimination
agrees with column elimination on its Jacobian rank2117 and inconsistency.
The same row code accepts the native Strassen positive control. Whole
Jacobian solutions and the compiler agree on the same64 candidate proposals;
raw derivative-image/residual checks and32 whole post-flip systems pass.
The full scans took15.1563s and28.6214s after imports. The code, proof,
native data, controls and costs are retained together.

Published plus/flip/Hensel search is the ordinary mechanism, not our
invention. Rational48 algorithms already exist. The small Python comparison
shows our quotient compilation is usable; it does not compare to optimized
incumbent implementations or establish a discovery advantage. The strongest
informed ordinary alternatives retain the same native data and the known
characteristic-zero48 construction.

The wave ends at a substantive scoped failure. Resume only with a genuine
new structural acquisition rule that escapes this boundary, or evidence
of repeatable successful repair under an equal-input, paid comparison.
There is no proposed physical experiment, model oracle, large-cluster
allocation or new autonomous search hidden in this conclusion.

# Costs, ordinary methods, and decision scope

The targeted capability was repeatable acquisition of small fast bilinear
algorithms from finite-field decompositions. A rank-47 rational 4-by-4 scheme
would be one possible output. It would not by itself beat the strongest
large-matrix exponent or optimized BLAS implementations. Addition count,
coefficient growth, recursion and floating-point error are separate costs.

The mechanism attempted here was exact obstruction-guided structural
rewriting. It was not an audit of the known native scheme: the actual
acquisition tested every one-plus expansion and every following flip,
including rank-48 intermediate decompositions, with unrestricted mod-4
corrections. All failed. General tangent-update algebra was constructed
and used to pay that finite search. No repaired characteristic-zero
algorithm, new rank bound, or practical speedup was obtained.

## Primary prior acquired before promotion

1. Fawzi et al., *Discovering faster matrix multiplication algorithms with
   reinforcement learning*, Nature 610 (2022), DOI
   [10.1038/s41586-022-05172-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-022-05172-4).
   Native factors and their cyclic output convention were acquired from
   [the official repository](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphatensor).
   Factorizations are available information; their discovery cost is not
   claimed as ours. Nonsoftware materials are CC-BY 4.0; attribution retained.

2. Kauers and Moosbauer, *Flip Graphs for Matrix Multiplication*, ISSAC 2023,
   [arXiv:2212.01175v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2212.01175v1), §5. They already
   give flip-graph search and Hensel lifting, and report that over 100000
   4-by-4 rank-47 schemes failed lifting from Z2 to Z4. Thus the native
   fixed-point obstruction and the broad strategy are prior, not discoveries
   here. Their successful lifts in other formats show why simply assuming
   all modular improvements transfer would be an incorrect interface.

3. Dumas, Pernet and Sedoglavic, *A non-commutative algorithm for multiplying
   4×4 matrices using 48 non-complex multiplications*,
